verdicts.flaw_description: The claim is about particulate readings, but every case reports backpressure (12, 9, 14 and 8 percent lower) - a pressure-drop measure, not an emissions measure. Lower backpressure across a filter is if anything consistent with a less restrictive element, so it does not show particulate levels fell.

The report states that prey abundance on the surrounding farmland 'doubled from the previous year' and that 'every box stood at the farmland edge, within the birds' foraging range' - so a doubling of food supply applies to all four plots and explains the extra 14, 11, 16 and 9 fledglings just as well as the boxes do.

The claim is about germination, but what was scored in all four lots is tetrazolium viability (9, 6, 11 and 7 points above the previous sowing) - a stain test of embryo viability, not a count of seeds that actually germinated. It is also an intrinsic property of the seed that an external coating would not change, especially since 'the seed batch was unchanged'.

The report says 'the board's pass mark fell a full grade below the previous term's, and every cohort sat the board's own paper under that same mark' - an easier pass threshold applied to all four cohorts and by itself raises pass rates, so the 7, 5, 8 and 4 point gains cannot be attributed to the tutoring blocks.
